title: Production spillover: cache-shadow corruption + memory-fragment surge causing GPU OOMs
creator: Asha Kumar
description: Summary: Multiple customer escalations across Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments were traced to a previously unseen interaction between the session KV layer and the GPU slab allocator. Under a particular traffic mix (many short chat sessions with intermittent long-context bursts) the KV layer created transient 'shadow' entries during prefix caching compaction. These shadows prevented proper slab reclamation and caused fragmentation that manifested as sudden GPU OOMs and degraded tail latency. Customers observed sudden session failures and elevated retry storms. This ticket tracks triage, mitigation, the runtime hotpatch rollout, and follow-up work.
symptoms_and_observed_behavior: Sporadic GPU OOMs on p3/p4 dedicated pools and hosted nodes between 2026-03-09 02:00 UTC and 2026-03-10 05:30 UTC
Tail latency increased for generation endpoints by 3-5x for affected sessions
KV eviction logs show compaction passes producing unexpected 'shadow' tombstones that remained pinned
OOMs correlated with workloads that had many short sessions but occasional >4k token continuations
steps_to_reproduce: Replay customer workload in an isolated staging cluster: 10k concurrent short sessions (<=64 tokens) with 2% of sessions issuing a long continuation (>4k tokens) after a pause
Enable full KV compaction debug logging and set allocator debug=fragmentation_trace
Observe allocator free-list never fully reclaiming slots corresponding to compacted prefixes; GPU memory usage grows non-linearly and final allocation fails
mitigation_and_workarounds: Immediate: rolled a conservative allocator fallback in hosted pool (runtime-2.4.0-alloc-guard) to avoid issuing large contiguous allocations when fragmentation threshold exceeded
Applied rate-limited session continuation guard in ingress to reduce bursty long-context continuations for affected customers (customer-facing temporary limit)
Advised Dedicated/Private customers to apply the hotpatch (runtime-2.4.1-hotpatch) and enable 'kv_strict_compact' feature flag
technical_root_cause: During parallel compaction the KV index reconciler created temporary tombstone 'shadow' references for prefix segments. A race between the compaction finalizer and the slab allocator's coalescer left pointers to freed KV slots in per-session slab lists. These dangling references prevented coalescer from reclaiming spans, causing slab fragmentation and large contiguous allocation failures on alloc-time, which surface as GPU OOMs under long-token continuations.
fix_summary: Implemented a two-part runtime fix: (1) make compaction finalizer atomic with respect to slab metadata updates; the finalizer now takes a lightweight per-prefix lock and clears shadow references before publishing compacted index entries, and (2) enhance the slab coalescer to detect and proactively sweep stale session pointers during coalescence. Added a defensive allocator path that retries allocations with on-the-fly local defragment and soft-evictions for low-priority KV entries.
deployments_and_rollout: Hotpatch build runtime-2.4.1-hotpatch created. Staged rollout: hosted Canary (10% of traffic) -> hosted Global (100%) -> Dedicated pools with staggered maintenance windows -> Private customers via private package and advisory. All rollouts use canary health checks and automated rollback on OOM rate increase >50% from baseline.
monitoring_and_observability: Added alert: SDK-ALERT-oom-spike if per-node GPU OOMs > 3 in 5 minutes or OOM-rate increases by >200%
Dashboards updated: /dashboards/runtime/kv-integrity and /dashboards/runtime/allocator-frag to show free-span histograms and active pointer counts
Added trace hooks to correlate allocation attempts with compaction events for retrospective analysis
customer_communications: Customer A (enterprise, dedicated): phone bridge opened 2026-03-09 06:00 UTC; provided hotpatch build and maintenance window; follow-up scheduled
Customer B (hosted): temporary ingress guard deployed and notice sent; confirmed recovery after canary rollout
Customer C (private/on-prem): provided patch bundle and debugging guidance; on-prem engineer engaged
blocking_issues_and_dependencies: Need security signoff for allocator soft-evict path when used with encrypted KV entries - SEC-2018
Compatibility check with quantized kernel memory model (infra-quant-test-2026) to ensure allocator changes don't regress inference kernels
postmortem_and_followups: Postmortem scheduled for 2026-03-20 with SRE, Runtime, and Customer Success
Follow-up: add E2E fuzz test for compaction+allocation races (owner: Diego Alvarez, estimate 8)
Follow-up: ship a telemetry sampler to capture fragile compaction windows for 30 days in production (owner: Priya Sen, estimate 5)
Follow-up: include compaction atomicity checks in release gating (CI)
notes_and_context: This bug surfaced after the recent compaction throughput improvements added in runtime-2.3; increased parallel compaction exposed a latent race
Work prioritization: P0 because multiple revenue customers experienced outages and because this can escalate quickly to broad OOM storms

Design trade-offs discussed: per-prefix locking reduces compaction throughput slightly for extreme workloads but provides a deterministic fix; we chose lightweight locking plus targeted defrag instead of a global stop-the-world compaction
next_steps: Complete rollouts for all hosted clusters by 2026-03-15 morning UTC
Coordinate Dedicated maintenance windows and confirm all committed pools are on hotpatch by 2026-03-18
Deliver private patch bundles and verify integrity with on-prem customers by 2026-03-21
Run post-deploy stress tests simulating mixed short/long session workloads for 72h
